{{Short description|How many of a graph's edges must be removed to increase domination number}}
[[File:Bondage number.svg|thumb|upright=1.3|The [[domination number]] of the graph on the left can be strictly increased by 1 when removing a minimum of 2 edges, shown on the right. The highlighted vertices show a minimum dominating set for each graph.]]
In the [[mathematical]] field of [[graph theory]], the '''bondage number''' of a nonempty [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] {{mvar|G}} is the [[cardinality]] of the smallest set of edges whose removal results in a [[domination number]] strictly greater than the domination number {{math|γ(''G'')}} of {{mvar|G}}. The bondage number is denoted {{math|''b''(''G'')}}.<ref name="fjkr90">{{cite journal | doi = 10.1016/0012-365X(90)90348-L | title=The bondage number of a graph | journal=Discrete Mathematics | date=1990 | volume=86 | issue=1–3 | pages=47–57 | first=John Frederick | last=Fink| author2=Michael S. Jacobson | author3=Lael F. Kinch | author4=John Roberts | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="hr94">{{cite journal | doi = 10.1016/0012-365X(94)90111-2 | title=Bounds on the bondage number of a graph | journal=Discrete Mathematics | date=1994 | volume=128 | issue=1–3 | pages=173–177 | first=Bert L. | last=Hartnell| doi-access= }}</ref>

The concept was introduced by Fink et al. in 1990 and measures the [[graph connectivity|vulnerability]] of a graph's domination structure to edge removal.<ref name="xu13">{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1155/2013/595210| title = On Bondage Numbers of Graphs: A Survey with Some Comments| journal = International Journal of Combinatorics| volume = 2013| issue = 1
| pages = 1–34| year = 2013| last1 = Xu | first1 = J. M. | doi-access = free| arxiv = 1204.4010}}</ref>

== Examples and specific values ==
For several standard families of graphs, exact values of the bondage number are known:<ref name="fjkr90"/>

*For the [[complete graph]] {{math|''K''<sub>''n''</sub>}} with {{math|''n'' ≥ 2}} vertices, {{math|1=''b''(''K''<sub>''n''</sub>) = ⌈''n''/2⌉}}.

*For the [[cycle graph]] {{math|''C''<sub>''n''</sub>}} with {{math|''n'' ≥ 3}} vertices, {{math|1=''b''(''C''<sub>''n''</sub>) = 3}} if {{math|1=''n'' ≡ 1 (mod 3)}}, and {{math|1=''b''(''C''<sub>''n''</sub>) = 2}} otherwise.

*For the [[path graph]] {{math|''P''<sub>''n''</sub>}} with {{math|''n'' ≥ 2}} vertices, {{math|1=''b''(''P''<sub>''n''</sub>) = 2}}.

*For nontrivial [[tree (graph theory)|trees]], the bondage number is at most 2. A tree has bondage number 1 if any vertex is adjacent to two or more [[leaf vertex|leaves]].
== Bounds ==
Several general bounds on the bondage number have been established. For a connected graph {{mvar|G}} of order {{mvar|p}} with maximum degree {{math|Δ(''G'')}} and minimum degree {{math|δ(''G'')}}, the following inequalities hold:<ref name="fjkr90"/><ref name="hr94"/>

*{{math|1=''b''(''G'') ≤ min<sub>{''u'',''v''} ∈ ''E''(''G'')</sub> (deg(''u'') + deg(''v'') − 1)}}

*{{math|1=''b''(''G'') ≤ Δ(''G'') + δ(''G'') − 1}}

*{{math|1=''b''(''G'') ≤ ''p'' − 1}}

*{{math|1=''b''(''G'') ≤ (γ(''G'') − 1)Δ(''G'') + 1}} if {{math|γ(''G'') ≥ 2}}

*{{math|1=''b''(''G'') ≤ ''p'' − γ(''G'') + 1}}, where {{math|γ(''G'')}} is the domination number

*{{math|1=''b''(''G'') ≤ λ(''G'') + Δ(''G'') − 1}}, where {{math|λ(''G'')}} is the edge connectivity

== Computational complexity ==
Determining the bondage number of a general graph is [[NP-hard]], as shown by Hu and Xu in 2012.<ref name="xu13"/> This hardness result has been strengthened to show that the bondage problem remains NP-hard even when restricted to [[bipartite graph]]s and even when asking whether {{math|1=''b''(''G'') ≤ 1}}.<ref name="hs14">{{cite journal | doi = 10.1016/j.tcs.2014.04.005| arxiv = 1403.2796| title=The algorithmic complexity of bondage and reinforcement problems in bipartite graphs | journal=Theoretical Computer Science | date=2014 | volume=535 | pages=46–53 | first=Fu-Tao | last=Hu| author2=Moo Young Sohn}}</ref> This is because if a polynomial time algorithm existed for computing bondage numbers, it could be used to compute domination numbers in polynomial time, which is known to be [[NP-complete]].

However, for special classes of graphs, efficient algorithms exist. In particular, the bondage number of any tree can be determined in [[Big O notation|O(''n'')]] time using a linear algorithm developed by Hartnell et al.<ref name="xu13"/>

== Conjectures ==
{{unsolved|mathematics|For the bondage number {{math|1=''b''(''G'')}} and maximum degree {{math|1=Δ(''G'')}} of a graph {{mvar|G}}, is {{math|1=''b''(''G'') ≤ (3/2)Δ(''G'')}} for all graphs?}}
A conjecture by Fink et al. from 1990 stated that for any nonempty graph {{mvar|G}},

:{{math|1=''b''(''G'') ≤ Δ(''G'') + 1}}.

However, this was disproved by Teschner in 1993, who showed that the [[Cartesian product of graphs|Cartesian product]] {{math|''K''<sub>3</sub> □ ''K''<sub>3</sub>}} has {{math|1=''b''(''K''<sub>3</sub> □ ''K''<sub>3</sub>) = Δ(''K''<sub>3</sub> □ ''K''<sub>3</sub>) + 2}}. More generally, Hartnell-Rall and Teschner independently showed that {{math|1=''b''(''K''<sub>''n''</sub> □ ''K''<sub>''n''</sub>) = (3/2)Δ(''K''<sub>''n''</sub> □ ''K''<sub>''n''</sub>)}} for {{math|''n'' ≥ 3}}.<ref name="hr94"/><ref name="xu13"/> They also provided a 4-regular [[bipartite graph]] with bondage number 6 as another counterexample.

Teschner then proposed the following weaker conjecture:<ref>{{cite journal |last=Teschner |first=Ulrich |date=1997 |title=New results about the bondage number of a graph |journal=Discrete Mathematics |volume=171 |issue=1–3 |pages=249–259 |doi=10.1016/S0012-365X(96)00007-6}}</ref>

:For any graph {{mvar|G}}, {{math|1=''b''(''G'') ≤ (3/2)Δ(''G'')}}.

This conjecture remains open.<ref name="xu13"/>

=== Planar graphs ===
For [[planar graph]]s, Dunbar et al. conjectured in 1998:

:If {{mvar|G}} is a planar graph, then {{math|1=''b''(''G'') ≤ Δ(''G'') + 1}}.

This conjecture has been verified for planar graphs with {{math|Δ(''G'') ≥ 7}} and for various other special cases, but remains open in general. It is known that {{math|1=''b''(''G'') ≤ min(8, Δ(''G'') + 2)}} for any connected planar graph {{mvar|G}}.<ref name="xu13"/>

== Variations ==
Several variations of the bondage number have been studied based on different types of domination. The '''total bondage number''' considers [[dominating set#Variants|total dominating set]]s (where every vertex in the dominating set must also be adjacent to another vertex in the dominating set).<ref name="hs14"/> The '''Roman bondage number''' is based on [[Roman dominating set|Roman domination]], where vertices are assigned values 0, 1, or 2 subject to certain constraints.<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.3934/math.2020397 | doi-access=free | title=Characterization of trees with Roman bondage number 1 | journal=AIMS Mathematics | date=2020 | volume=5 | issue=6 | pages=6183–6188 | first=Fu-Tao | last=Hu| author2=Xing Wei Wang | author3=Ning Li}}</ref> Further generalizations include the '''double Roman bondage number''',<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1142/S179383092250046X | title=On the double Roman bondage numbers of graphs | journal=Discrete Mathematics, Algorithms and Applications | date=2022 | volume=14 | issue=8 | pages=2250046 | first=N. | last=Jafari Rad| author2=H. R. Maimani | author3=M. Momeni | author4=F. Rahimi Mahid| arxiv=1905.06724 }}</ref> the '''independent Roman bondage number''',<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1051/ro/2023017 | doi-access=free | title=Independent Roman bondage of graphs | journal=RAIRO Operations Research | date=2023 | volume=57 | pages=371–382 | first=Saeed | last=Kosari| author2=Jafar Amjadi | author3=Mustapha Chellali | author4=Seyed Mahmoud Sheikholeslami}}</ref> and the '''quasi-total Roman bondage number'''.<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1080/09728600.2022.2098876 | doi-access=free | title=Quasi-total Roman bondage number in graphs | journal=AKCE International Journal of Graphs and Combinatorics | date=2022 | volume=19 | issue=3 | pages=221–228 | first=Huiqin | last=Jiang| author2=Zehui Shao}}</ref> Other variations include the '''k-power bondage number''',<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1142/S1793830916500646 | title=The k-power bondage number of a graph | journal=Discrete Mathematics, Algorithms and Applications | date=2016 | volume=8 | issue=4 | pages=1650064 | first=Seethu | last=Varghese| author2=A. Vijayakumar}}</ref> the '''cobondage number''',<ref>{{cite journal | title=The cobondage number of a graph | journal=Discussiones Mathematicae Graph Theory | date=1996 | volume=16 | issue=2 | pages=111–117 | first=V. R. | last=Kulli| author2=B. Janakiram | url=http://eudml.org/doc/270364|ISSN = 2083-5892}}</ref> and the '''lower bondage number'''.<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1051/ro/2015062| url =  https://www.numdam.org/item/10.1051/ro/2015062.pdf| title=On the average lower bondage number of a graph | journal=RAIRO Operations Research | date=2016 | volume=50 | pages=1003–1012 | first=Tufan | last=Turaci}}</ref>

== Motivation ==
The bondage number has applications in analyzing the vulnerability of communication networks. In a network modeled as a graph where vertices represent sites and edges represent direct communication links, a minimum dominating set corresponds to an optimal placement of transmitters so that every site either has a transmitter or is directly connected to a site with a transmitter. The bondage number represents the minimum number of communication links that must fail before an additional transmitter is required to maintain communication with all sites.<ref name="fjkr90"/>

== Related problems ==
The '''reinforcement number''' {{math|''r''(''G'')}} is the minimum number of edges that must be added to {{mvar|G}} to decrease its domination number. Like the bondage number, determining the reinforcement number is NP-hard even for bipartite graphs.<ref name="hs14"/>
